guide.title: How to set up OBS
guide.step1: Use OBS Studio 30 or newer: Settings → Stream
guide.step3: Server: paste the template's server URL
guide.step4: Bearer Token: paste your stream secret
guide.step5: Start Streaming in OBS. You're live on 3Speak.
guide.chatCopy: At the top of this page, under "Your chat in OBS", click "Copy chat URL". It is one link for all your streams.
guide.chat2: In OBS, open the "Docks" menu and choose "Custom Browser Docks". Enter a name like "3Speak chat", paste the URL and click "Apply". New messages show up in that panel while you are live. Viewers never see it.
guide.chat3: Viewers already see the chat next to your stream, so you don't need to put it into the video. Only if you also share the stream somewhere else: add the same URL as a "Browser" source and remove "&dock=1" from its end. Then the messages float over the video and fade out after 30 seconds.
guide.chatOptions: Optional, add to the end of the URL: &max=10 shows fewer lines, &size=18 makes the text bigger, &fade=0 keeps messages on the video.
guide.limitsFree: Free streams end after 30 minutes and show a 3Speak watermark. With 3Speak Pro you can stream for 4 hours without a watermark.
guide.limitsPro: With 3Speak Pro your streams can run for 4 hours and carry no watermark.

phoneSource.menuHint: Show the screen of an iPhone, iPad or Android device: mirror it to this computer, then share that window
phoneSource.title: Phone or tablet screen
phoneSource.lead: Mirror the phone to this computer, then share that window. Nothing goes through other services.
phoneSource.pictureHeading: Get the phone onto this computer
phoneSource.shareText: Pick the window that shows the phone.
phoneSource.airplayMacD: Same Wi-Fi for both. On the iPhone or iPad: Control Centre → Screen Mirroring → this Mac (macOS 12 or newer).
phoneSource.airplayReceiverD: Same Wi-Fi for both. On the iPhone or iPad: Control Centre → Screen Mirroring → pick the receiver.
phoneSource.quicktimeD: QuickTime Player → File → New Movie Recording → pick the iPhone or iPad as the camera.
phoneSource.receiverWinD: Windows can't receive AirPlay by itself. Get a free receiver app from the Microsoft Store (search “AirPlay receiver”) and open it.
phoneSource.receiverLinuxD: UxPlay is a free AirPlay receiver (package “uxplay”). Start it:
phoneSource.scrcpyWinD: Free. Download the Windows zip and unpack it.
phoneSource.scrcpyLinuxD: Free. Take the newest version: the package in your distribution can be too old for new phones.
phoneSource.devD: On the phone (Android 11 or newer): Settings → About phone → tap Build number 7 times. Then Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code.
phoneSource.pairD: With the address and code from the pairing popup:
phoneSource.connectD: With the address under “IP address & port” on the Wireless debugging screen (not the pairing port):
phoneSource.startD: The phone's screen opens in a window.
phoneSource.cableD: Turn on USB debugging in the developer options, plug the phone in and run scrcpy.
phoneSource.castD: Many phones can: Settings → System → Optional features → add Wireless Display, open it, then Cast or Smart View from the phone.
phoneSource.soundWinT: Share a second time, for the sound
phoneSource.soundWinD: Click Share the window again, choose Entire screen and switch on “Share system audio”. Keep the phone window as the picture: the second share only brings the sound.
phoneSource.soundMacD: A Mac browser can't take another app's sound. Install a free virtual audio device (BlackHole, for example), make it the Mac's sound output, then in the studio: Add source → Desktop / aux audio → BlackHole.
phoneSource.sinkPickD: Add source → Desktop / aux audio → “Monitor of Phone”. Reload the studio if it isn't listed yet.
